headline: The shorts collapse reversed: weekly views went 697 (Aug 22–28) → 1,237 (Aug 29–Sep 4) → 1,440 in just Sep 5–6, driven by two 4-digit shorts — 'Name one programmer better than Fable. We couldn't.' (1,170 views, 4 comments, 69% AVD) and 'Will Smith eating spaghetti, 2026 edition' (933 in ~1 day). Neither is a money/greed hook; last week's 'go back to money' thesis is not supported (the two money picks, 'API credits? Cooked' and '11 downloads, $0', landed 50 and 58). Long-form packaging is fixed and retention is not: Ep 12 and Ep 13 launched at 2.05% and 2.24% CTR (best on the channel; Ep 10 was 0.54%) and Ep 12 is the most-viewed episode since Ep 3 (287 views), but avg view % fell to 7.25% / 8.43% (Ep 9–11 were 15–20%) — 71% of Ep 12 viewers are gone by 1:05 and 93% by 5:29, exactly across the 3-min tokenomics tangent kept ahead of the perp reveal. Subs 22 → 24 but the 30-day daily ledger is still +5/−6, and SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS is still exactly 5 lifetime views after ~3,800 more shorts views: the funnel checklist has now been skipped for six episodes. Two levers this week: wire the funnel on the live 1,170-view short today (or kill the checklist as a process), and in the edit, never leave more than ~60 s between the title card and the first payoff.

production.title: Funnel still dead — SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS 5 → 5 across ~3,800 new shorts views; run it once on Ep 13's 8 shorts or retire the checklist
production.evidence: Traffic-source deltas 8/26 → 9/9: SHORTS +2,532 views, YT_SEARCH +211, YT_OTHER_PAGE +115, RELATED_VIDEO +23, SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS +0 (5 lifetime, 1 minute). Ep 11 batch (7 shorts) 643 views, Ep 12 batch (7) 934 views, Ep 13 batch (4 live) 2,262 views — zero of them produced a tracked click to long-form. The live winner 'Name one programmer better than Fable' (o_TzYAKzONk) has 1,170 views and 4 comments and no pinned comment. Ep 12 sheet and Ep 13 sheet both still say 'Funnel checklist owed'.
production.recommendation: Today, in Studio, on o_TzYAKzONk and oQywbcmQ8xA (the two live breakouts) plus the 6 other Ep 13 shorts as they publish: related-video → Ep 13, pinned comment with youtu.be/36HwFHzF6sM?t=342 (Fable short) / ?t=1048 (spaghetti), reply to the 4 comments. Treat it as the one-shot test the memory has owed since Ep 7: if SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS is still <10 at the 9/23 pull, retire the checklist (Jackson's rule: kill processes that don't work) and rely on the description link + branded ender.
production.status_note: reopened unchanged for the 3rd week; data proves it was not run for Ep 12 (7 shorts) or Ep 13 (4 live shorts). Converted to a time-boxed test with a kill date.

production.title: Hook thesis revised: provocation + meme anchor won, money hooks didn't — rebalance Ep 14 picks
production.evidence: Ep 13 batch: 'Name one programmer better than Fable' 1,170v (36 impressions → shorts-feed distribution, not browse) · 'Will Smith eating spaghetti, 2026 edition' 933v · 'You're a genius, email Stanford' 101v · 'I asked Fable to make me $1M. 11 downloads, $0' 58v. Ep 12 batch: 'Frozen peas saved this podcast' 407v · Pitbull roommate 118v · 'February is a different decade' 118v · recruiter cult 111v · agent heaven 73v · Roomba 57v · 'API credits? Cooked beyond belief' 50v. Ep 11 tail: 'Please don't deport me, Brian' 303v — the callback joke last week's note said to hold. Both money-lever picks finished bottom-3 of their batch. Channel-wide, every 4-digit short is a ≤6-word premise a non-crypto viewer can parse instantly: lottery ticket, egg allergy, Halo 3 roast, dice 100 times, Fable programmer, spaghetti.
production.recommendation: Ep 14 picks (7–8 shorts): 3 provocation hooks (a disagreeable claim about AI/money in ≤10 words), 2 meme/physical-comedy anchors, ≤2 money/perp one-liners, 0 earnest explainers. Keep titles as the claim itself, not a description ('MCPs were a waste of time (I built one)' is the right shape; 'What do you promise an AI agent in heaven?' is not). Length: the two breakouts are 17 s and 22 s; keep the 10–20 s target.
production.status_note: last week's item said 'bias 4-of-7 to money/greed/gambling'. Ep 12's picks were 2 money / 3 comedy / 2 explainer; the money ones flopped and comedy + provocation carried both batches. Thesis corrected, not carried forward.

production.title: Ep 12 kept a 3-min tangent between perp setup and reveal for PiP monotonicity — it cost 3/4 of the remaining audience
production.evidence: Ep 12 retention: 74% at 0:32 → 29% at 1:05 (title card) → 16% at 2:44 → 7% at 5:29. The 1:01–5:31 span is 'Perp of Fortune: max long DOGE' (1:01) then 'Tyler's tokenomics tangent: MV = PQ' (2:33–5:31) with the reveal at 5:31. The sheet's edit note says chronological order was kept because 'PiP monotonicity forbids moving the tangent after the reveal.' vs_typical over 2:44–8:14 is 0.09–0.17, the worst stretch on any episode this summer. Ep 12 avg view % 7.25% vs Ep 11 18.13%, Ep 9 19.76%; 287 views produced 405 watch-min (Ep 9: 80 views, 887 min).
production.recommendation: Edit rule for Ep 14: nothing longer than 60 s sits between the title card and the first payoff (perp reveal or marquee hook). If that means the PiP restarts or the tangent moves post-reveal, do it — dashboard continuity is worth less than 22 points of retention at the 10% mark. Also try no hard title card: logo bug + title lower-third over the first segment, since the :56 card coincides with a −45pp / −49pp / −53pp step on Ep 12 / 13 / 11.

production.title: Ep 13 retitled after the sheet was written — undocumented again (Ep 10 repeat); backfill the log
production.evidence: Live title in today's pull: 'Is AGI Already Here?'. episodes/ep13/segment-times.md (commit e9c4490, 9/4) says live title = 'Google Defined AGI. We Graded Fable as Superhuman'. Ep 13 reach is the best launch CTR on the channel (2.24% on 1,963 impressions at 6 days) but there is no record of which title earned it or when the switch happened. Ep 10's undocumented retitle is logged in memory as the reason its 0.54% CTR could never be debugged.
production.recommendation: Add a dated log line to segment-times.md → Episode video ('Retitled YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC: from X to Y, reason'). Going forward, retitle through yt_upload.py/videos.update so the change is scripted and self-documenting. Also check whether the live description still says 'Fable' in the first line now that the title doesn't.

production.title: Subs 22 → 24, but still flat on the 30-day ledger; LIKE+SUBSCRIBE overlay shipped in Ep 13 — too early to grade
production.evidence: Daily 8/8–9/6: +5 / −6 (net −1). Events since last pull: 8/30 +1/−1, 8/31 −1, 9/3 +1 (Ep 13 launch), 9/6 +1. Per-video subs_gained since 8/26: Ep 13 long-form +1 (210 views, 0.48%), 'Banks Should Spy on You Act' short +1 (57 views); the 1,170-view Fable short +0, spaghetti +0. Shorts → subs across ~3,800 views: 1 (0.03%, unchanged from last week's 0.04%). Ep 13 is the first episode with the on-screen LIKE+SUBSCRIBE overlay (2:24 and 52:05); Ep 12 had none and got 0 subs from 287 views.
production.recommendation: Keep the overlay in Ep 14 and grade it on a 2-episode sample. The shorts-side sub lever is still the funnel item above; nothing else in the data points at a cheaper one.
production.status_note: overlay shipped (Ep 13 commit 6eaadf7). Sub count moved +2 but not attributably; keep open.

production.title: Ep 11 packaging retro-fix: closed, window expired
production.evidence: Ep 11 finished at 1,254 impressions / 1.59% CTR / 44 views (from 1,090 / 1.56% / 33 on 8/26). ~95% of lifetime impressions land in week one, so the A/B was unrunnable by the time it was proposed. The lesson landed anyway: Ep 12 shipped with the thumbnail.py house recipe and launched at 2.05% CTR on 2,927 impressions, Ep 13 at 2.24% on 1,963.
production.recommendation: No action. Packaging is a launch-day gate; the two launches since prove the recipe works. Next packaging problem is retention, not CTR.
production.status_note: closed 9/9 as expired; the Ep 12/13 launch CTRs supersede it.

production.title: Aug 26–28 shorts resequence/burst: not done, and the callback joke won anyway
production.evidence: They ran on the original schedule. 'Please don't deport me, Brian' 303 views (best of the Ep 11 batch), 'Three AIs, zero knew what we bought' 136, 'Banks Should Spy on You Act' 57 (+1 sub). Last week predicted Brian would need context and 'Three AIs' was the closest to a money hook. Wrong on both.
production.recommendation: None; fold into the revised hook thesis above. Do not spend time resequencing scheduled batches — the ordering signal is smaller than the pick signal.
production.status_note: closed 9/9; prediction falsified, lesson merged into the hook item.

production.title: SUBSCRIBER traffic source +326 views / +465 min in 14 days on a 24-sub base — verify it isn't host rewatch
production.evidence: SUBSCRIBER went 644 → 970 views, 1,891 → 2,356 min. Ep 12 + Ep 13 long-form together account for 673 watch-min in the same window, so most long-form watch time is arriving via subscriber surfaces. 326 views from 24 subscribers is ~13 views each, which is more consistent with hosts checking the live copy than with organic sub behavior. If so, Ep 12's 287 views overstate reach and its 7.25% retention is partly QA sessions bailing early.
production.recommendation: Check Studio → Ep 12 → traffic source → Subscriptions for the daily shape (spiky on 8/28–8/29 = hosts). If confirmed, QA the live copy logged out or in a non-subscribed profile from Ep 14 on, so the launch-week numbers stay clean.

recording.title: Finale tease in the cold open worked (Ep 13 held 40.7% at 1:03 vs 29.0% / 27.8% for Ep 12 / 11) — then the check-in halved it
recording.evidence: Ep 13 cold open beat 2 was the egg-app reveal (teases the 44:44 finale), the [rec] experiment from last week. Retention at 1:03: Ep 13 40.7%, Ep 12 29.0%, Ep 11 27.8%, Ep 10 55.2%, Ep 9 46.2%. Then 1:01–2:37 is 'Goblin mode: Tyler's out' and retention falls 40.7% → 25.4% (1:35) → 20.3% (2:39); the perp doesn't start until 2:37 and the marquee until 5:42, by which point 15.2% remain (Ep 11 had 25.0% at the same mark). This is the exact failure named last week: dropping back into check-ins after the cold open.
recording.recommendation: Keep the finale tease as a fixed beat. Move the check-in: title card → perp reveal (or the marquee's first shocking line) inside 60 s → then the check-in as a breather. If a host is out, one line ('Tyler's in goblin mode, we'll survive') and move on; the 90-second riff belongs after the first payoff.

recording.title: Get to the perp reveal in ≤90 s from when the segment starts — Ep 12's 3-min setup lost 29% → 7%
recording.evidence: Ep 12: perp opens 1:01, MV=PQ tangent 2:33–5:31, reveal 5:31. Retention 29% (1:05) → 16% (2:44) → 12% (3:50) → 7% (5:29). The edit could not save it (PiP constraint, see production). Ep 13 did the reveal at 4:12 (+$0.10 gag) and held 20.3% → 15.2% across the same window — better, still a leak. Ep 9, the best-retaining episode of the summer, was at 32.5% / 27.5% at the 5% / 10% marks.
recording.recommendation: On mic: state the trade, the thesis in one sentence, open the dashboard, react. Tangents (tokenomics, Pitbull lore, math camp) go after the number is on screen. Target: 10% mark ≥ 20% on Ep 14.

recording.title: Provocation is the clip engine — one disagreeable, quotable claim per segment
recording.evidence: 'How many people do you know who are a better programmer than Fable? — I know zero' → 1,170 views and 4 comments (the first short with comments since 8/8). 'MCPs were a waste of time (I built one)' is the same shape and publishes 9/11. 'Shots fired at lawyers AND accountants' publishes 9/9. Money-lever one-liners ('cooked beyond belief', '11 downloads, $0') got 50 and 58. Meme anchors (spaghetti 933, frozen peas 407) are the second engine and come from physical bits, not scripting.
recording.recommendation: Replace last week's 'money/greed line per segment' standing note with: every segment lands one claim a stranger could argue with in the comments, said in ≤10 words, with the show or a host named in the same breath. Keep doing the physical bits on camera (peas, spaghetti, reaction inserts) — they clip.

recording.title: Don't record segments the hosts already think are dead — Ep 13's Euro stablecoin ran 3 min at vs_typical 0.11
recording.evidence: Ep 13 vs_typical by segment: 'Who AI hurts first' (24:38–31:21) 0.64 at the 50% mark, the best mid-episode marker on the channel; 'Astra vs GLM-5.3' + 'Euro stablecoin' (35:03–44:44) 0.19 → 0.11 at the 70–80% marks; the finale (chicken app, 44:44→) recovers to 0.40–0.44. Ep 12: 'NVIDIA buys the crime scene' (22:25–31:02) sits at vs_typical 0.06 at the 50% mark; 'Harness wars' 0.19–0.21. Both episodes' best segments were the ones with a person in them (sycophancy stories, the agent cult); the worst were the market/industry analysis blocks.
recording.recommendation: If a host says 'I said that it sucks' about a topic on the prep guide, cut it from the slate rather than paying a 3-minute debt on tape. Cap pure industry-analysis segments at ~6 min and anchor each in a human story (a user, a victim, a founder) within the first 30 s — that is the pattern in the 0.64 segment.

recording.title: Perp-rides-all-episode still holds the ending; keep it structural
recording.evidence: Ep 12 retention is flat at 5–6% from 43:58 to the end card (vs_typical 0.37 → 0.44); Ep 13 flat at 5.1% from 47:59 (vs_typical 0.25 → 0.44). The reaction inserts (whenItHits6 at 46:35, ending.mov at 53:03) sit inside the best-held stretch of Ep 13. Two green weeks on the board (+$7.30, +$6.71) give the arc a story to tell into Ep 14.
recording.recommendation: Keep it. Ep 14: open the pip on the reveal, ride to the end, and put the streak (three in a row or the break) on the end card as the promised finale. Tyler's return is a natural check-in beat, but see item 1 — it goes after the reveal.
